description: The three-codes block of every chapter of the Book of DOSE: per country, the pack barcode, the national pack code and the authorisation number as the regulator publishes them, each with the page it was read from and the date. A line that was not found on a regulator's page is unknown.

auth.text: Each registered drug has a registration number held in the Ministry of Health's drug registration system, which the national tracking platform requires in product data.

gtin.text: The Ministry of Health's serialisation guide requires every secondary pack to carry a 2D barcode that encodes the Global Trade Item Number (GTIN), listed first among required data.

auth.text: Argentina's regulator certifies each medicine's entry in the Registro de Especialidades Medicinales with a certificate of registration carrying a number.

gtin.text: Argentina's traceability system requires each medicine pack to carry a Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) together with a serial number.

auth.text: Austrian authorisations carry a Zulassungsnummer such as 1-123456, and parallel-import authorisations add a suffix like -P01 to the number of the original authorisation.

pack.text: Austria identifies each medicine pack with a national number called the Pharmazentralnummer (PZN), for which the federal office's page refers applicants to the body that assigns it.

auth.text: Australia requires a medicine's registration or listing number on its label, preceded by the prefix AUST R for registered goods or AUST L for listed goods.
The Bulgarian Drug Agency gives each authorised medicine a registration number, which applicants must quote on fee payments; its digit format is not stated.
Anvisa assigns a registration number to each medicine presentation, which its tracing system handles as a 13-character field.

gtin.text: Anvisa's medicine tracing rules require each medicine pack presentation to carry a 14-digit Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) inside its unique medicine identifier.

auth.text: Health Canada assigns each authorised drug product an eight-digit Drug Identification Number (DIN), shown on the label of prescription and over-the-counter products.
Swissmedic gives each authorised medicine an authorisation number, shown in its guidance as a five-digit number such as 41557.

gtin.text: Swiss packaging rules require a Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) barcode on the outer pack of authorised medicines, and the authorisation number is usually built into it.

pack.text: Swissmedic identifies each pack by the authorisation number plus a packaging code, which must appear on the outer pack, shown for example as 41557 001.

auth.text: Chile records each registered medicine under a numbered sanitary registration kept in a special sequential roll by the Instituto de Salud Pública.
The regulator issues a registro sanitario for each authorised product and lets the public check its validity and status online.

gtin.text: Colombia's regulator requires the Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) from the product's barcode to be entered in its data standard for medicine applications.

pack.text: The regulator assigns one Identificador Único de Medicamento to each medicine presentation; printing it on packs is not required.

auth.text: The regulator numbers each national marketing authorisation in the form AA/BBBB/XX-C or S/C; centrally authorised products carry the EU number instead.

gtin.text: Czech medicine packs carry a product code that may be a Global Trade Item Number (GTIN); the regulator does not issue it, and rules allow an EAN or 2D code.

pack.text: The regulator gives each pack presentation a seven-digit SÚKL code, which must be shown on the packaging.

auth.text: Each authorised finished medicine has a Zulassungsnummer, which the law requires on its labelling under the abbreviation Zul.-Nr.

pack.text: Germany uses the Pharmazentralnummer, a nationwide pack identification key issued by the information service for medicines, not by the authorisation authority.

auth.text: Denmark gives each marketing authorisation a number called the MT-nr. (markedsføringstilladelsesnummer), on which the Danish Medicines Agency charges its annual fee.

pack.text: Danish medicine packs must carry a varenummer (product number), which identifies the individual pack and which the authorisation holder can request from the Danish Medicines Agency.

auth.text: The medicines regulator grants a Registro Sanitario, a sanitary registration, that allows a medicine to be sold in the Dominican Republic.
The national health regulator gives each authorised medicine a sanitary registration number, which must be printed on the final label; its format is not stated.
The State Agency of Medicines lists each newly authorised medicine with a marketing authorisation number, a numeric code such as a seven-digit number.

pack.text: The State Agency of Medicines register holds a unique code for each pack size, used in e-prescriptions and pharmacy databases, but it is virtual and not printed on the pack.
Each pack of a human medicine must be given a unique identification number issued by the Egyptian Drug Authority's national electronic track-and-trace system.

auth.text: The Spanish medicines agency assigns a número de registro to authorised medicines and presentations, which it generates for each centrally authorised medicine on request.

pack.text: Spain's national pack code is the Código Nacional (CN), written as six digits plus a check digit, which the medicines agency assigns to each pack.

auth.text: A centrally authorised medicine gets an EU number made of the type, the last two digits of the year, a chronological product number and a package presentation number.

pack.text: In the Union Register's EU number, the last segment is a number given to each individual package presentation of the centrally authorised product.
France identifies each medicine pack by a 13-digit presentation identifier code (CIP13), which is stated in the marketing authorisation decision.

auth.text: Ghana's Food and Drugs Authority gives each registered product a registration number, which locally manufactured products must show on their labels.

pack.text: The Greek medicines agency lists each pack under a 13-digit barcode number in its published product lists, shown next to the product description and authorisation holder.

auth.text: Croatia's medicines database shows each authorised medicine with an approval number, written HR-H- followed by nine digits.

pack.text: Croatia's medicines database gives each pack its own approval number, made of the medicine's approval number plus a two-digit pack suffix.

auth.text: BPOM issues each medicine a marketing authorisation number, the Nomor Izin Edar, made of 15 letters and digits.
The Health Products Regulatory Authority gives each authorised medicine a PA number written as the letters PA followed by three numbers separated by slashes.
Italy's marketing authorisation (AIC) number is a numeric code of six digits that uniquely identifies a medicine.

pack.text: In Italy each pack carries a 9-digit AIC code, the 6-digit AIC number followed by three further digits identifying the pack.

auth.text: The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare gives each approved product an approval number of digits and letters, whose last three digits are a sub-number.

gtin.text: The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare requires prescription-medicine packs to carry a Global Trade Item Number (GTIN): GTIN-13 for dispensing packs, GTIN-14 for sales packs and outer cases.

auth.text: The Pharmacy and Poisons Board's public register gives each registered product a Product Registration No in three slash-separated parts, such as H2026/CTD13490/29699.

pack.text: Korea's drug database lists one or more standard codes for each product, one per pack, alongside the product item code.

auth.text: Authorised medicines are entered in the EEA medicines register in the applicant's name and identified by a number.
The Medicines Authority gives every medicine authorised for sale in Malta an authorisation number, which must appear on the outer carton.
Mexico's labelling standard requires the medicine's sanitary registration key to be shown on the label exactly as it appears in the registration.
Malaysia gives every registered drug a registration number starting with MAL, which must be printed on its label or package.
Nigeria's regulator issues a registration number, recorded on the registration certificate, once a drug application completes its approval stages.

gtin.text: Nigeria's traceability regulations require the Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) in the unique identifier on primary and secondary medicine packs.

auth.text: The Medicines Evaluation Board registers each medicine under a unique registration number called an RVG or RVH number, entered in the information bank as digits only.

pack.text: Norway requires the Nordic article number, printed as Vnr followed by six digits in three pairs, at least once on the outer packaging.

auth.text: Each registered medicine has a sanitary registration number, which the law makes mandatory on container labels.
Peru authorises each medicine through a sanitary registration number, shown in the regulator's notices as two letters, a hyphen and five digits.
Each medicine has a marketing authorisation, called a pozwolenie na dopuszczenie do obrotu, which also sets the identification number printed on each pack.

gtin.text: Polish authorisations assign each pack an identification number (EAN/GTIN), and government guidance says it is printed on packs and may not differ from the one in the authorisation.

pack.text: In Portugal each pack presentation has a Número de Registo assigned by INFARMED, which must be added as extra data in the unique identifier on the pack.

auth.text: Each pack in Romania's register shows the marketing authorisation number, year and a pack suffix, for example 7321/2015/01.

pack.text: Romania's medicines register lists a Cod CIM for each pack presentation, shown as a letter W followed by eight digits.

auth.text: The Saudi Food and Drug Authority's list of registered drugs gives a registration number for each registered drug; its format is not stated.

gtin.text: The Saudi Food and Drug Authority's track-and-trace system tracks each drug pack by a Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) and a serial number in a two-dimensional barcode.

pack.text: Swedish packs carry a Nordic article number, written as Vnr followed by three pairs of characters, on the label of nearly all medicines.

auth.text: The Health Sciences Authority gives each registered therapeutic product a product registration number made of SIN, digits and the letter P.
The central database shows the number of the latest marketing authorisation and the date it was issued.

gtin.text: Slovenia's central medicines database records for each pack its EAN barcode, which the page describes as carrying the Global Trade Item Number (GTIN).

pack.text: Slovenia's agency assigns a national medicine code that uniquely identifies a medicine by form, strength, pack and supplier.

auth.text: Slovakia's register shows each registered medicine with a registration number, for example 36/0053/13-S.

gtin.text: Slovakia requires the pack's Global Trade Item Number (GTIN-14 format) as the product code inside the 2D code on the outer pack.

pack.text: Slovakia's medicines register gives each pack presentation a ŠÚKL code, which can be searched directly in the regulator's database.

auth.text: Thai medicine labels show the registration number of the medicine formula, written as an English-letter prefix, a sequence number and the Buddhist Era year of registration.
Türkiye's licensing regulation lists a licence number (ruhsat numarası) among the details recorded for each licensed human medicinal product.

gtin.text: Türkiye's medicine tracking rules require each pack's 2D code to include its Global Trade Item Number (GTIN), which identifies every pack size worldwide.

auth.text: Each registered medicine in the state register has a registration certificate number, shown in the form UA/ plus three numeric groups.
The UK regulator issues each marketing authorisation a PL number, which must be obtained before applying for the licence.
The FDA identifies an approved drug by its NDA or ANDA application number, which shows the product has been approved for marketing.

pack.text: The FDA's National Drug Code is a 10-digit number in three segments that identifies the labeler, the product and the package size.

auth.text: Vietnam's Pharmacy Law requires medicine labels to show the circulation registration number, or the import licence number for imported medicines.
Each registered medicine is allocated a registration number under section 15(6) of the Medicines Act, which must appear on its label.

gtin.text: The regulator's traceability guideline requires a Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) to be assigned to each packaging level and carried in a 2D barcode on packs.
